Introduction

OPT-2A is an optical tube leveling amplifier. Inside a classic opto compressor a small light panel glows brighter as the signal gets louder, and a light-sensitive cell turns the level down. Light cells are slow and a little lazy, so the compression is smooth and natural: it grabs quickly, lets go fast at first and then slowly over a second or two. That is why this kind of compressor is famous on vocals, bass and anything that needs to sit steadily in a mix without sounding squashed.

OPT-2A was built by measuring a tube opto leveler with test signals (steady tones at many levels and frequencies, bursts, sweeps and noise) and fitting every part of the model to the results: how much it compresses at each Peak Reduction setting, the attack and the two-stage release, the slight lift in the top end, the tube output stage and the soft harmonics it adds.

Quick start

  1. Insert OPT-2A on a track or bus. It loads with Peak Reduction 25, Gain 30, Compress and the meter on Gain Reduction.
  2. Play your audio and turn Peak Reduction up until the needle moves left by the amount of leveling you want (about 3–6 dB for a natural vocal, more for an obvious, thick sound).
  3. Use Gain to bring the level back up. Switch the meter to Output +4 to set the output by eye, or click Power to compare with the plugin off.
  4. Need parallel compression? Turn Mix down to blend in the uncompressed signal.
Like the hardware, OPT-2A has gain even when it isn't compressing: at the default Gain 30 it is about +5.6 dB louder. Gain 17 is roughly unity (0 dB).

Controls

1Peak Reduction

The main control. It sets how strongly the light cell is driven, so turning it up gives more compression. There is no separate threshold or ratio: like the original, the higher you turn it, the lower the point where leveling starts.

SettingLeveling starts around (sine peak)Typical use
0—No compression, just the tube colour
25−13 dBFSLight touch on peaks
40−21 dBFSGentle vocal / bass leveling
55−28 dBFSSteady, upfront vocals
70−36 dBFSHeavy, thick leveling
90+−47 dBFSEffect, squashed sound

Above that point the output rises only about 1 dB for every 4–5 dB of input, with a soft knee.

2Gain

The output (make-up) gain of the tube amplifier. Every 10 steps is about +4.3 dB: 0 ≈ −7 dB, 17 ≈ 0 dB, 30 ≈ +5.6 dB, 60 ≈ +18.4 dB.

Gain also drives the tube output stage. Clean below 0 dBFS, it starts to saturate softly above it, adding mostly 3rd-order harmonics with a little 2nd, and it can never go much past about +6 dBFS. Push it on purpose for grit and density.

3Limit / Compress switch

Down = Compress (default): a softer curve, about 4:1–5:1, transparent and musical.

Up = Limit: a firmer curve that flattens peaks almost completely at high levels. Use it to catch peaks hard or for an aggressive, in-your-face sound.

4Emphasis (FLAT → HF)

A small screw that adds treble to what the compressor listens to (not to what you hear). At FLAT it reacts to the full range. Turning it towards HF (up to +12 dB above about 3 kHz) makes bright sounds compress more, which tames harsh "s" sounds and cymbals and lets the bass breathe.

5Mix

Blends the leveled signal with the uncompressed one (100 = fully compressed). Both paths go through the same tube stage, so the tone stays consistent. Values around 40–70 give classic parallel compression: thick but still punchy.

6VU meter

A real VU-style needle with about 300 ms of ballistics.

  • In Gain Reduction mode the needle rests at 0 and moves left as the level is turned down: −3 means 3 dB of reduction.
  • In the Output modes it shows the output level.
  • With Power off the needle falls to the left stop.

7Meter selector

Chooses what the needle shows:

  • GAIN REDUCTION (centre): how much the cell is turning the level down.
  • OUTPUT +4 (right): output level, 0 VU = −18 dBFS RMS. Good for typical mixing levels.
  • OUTPUT +10 (left): output level, 0 VU = −12 dBFS RMS, for hotter signals.

8Waveform display

A scrolling picture of the last ~2 seconds:

  • IN (grey): the signal going in.
  • OUT (amber): the signal coming out. Where the grey sticks out above the amber, those peaks are being turned down.
  • GR (red line): gain reduction. The line dips as the compressor works, and you can see the fast-then-slow optical release as it rises back.

9Power

Click the red lamp (or the word POWER) to switch OPT-2A on or off. Off is a clean bypass with a short crossfade, so it's perfect for A/B comparisons. Match the levels with Gain first so the louder version doesn't fool your ears.

10? – Manual

Opens this manual in your web browser. You can also right-click anywhere on the panel and choose Open manual…

How it sounds

  • Attack: fast. Most of the reduction happens within a few milliseconds, then it settles over the next 20–200 ms. Small amounts of compression come in more slowly than big ones.
  • Release, two stages: about half of the reduction lets go in roughly 60–100 ms, and the rest drifts back over 0.5–2 seconds. After long, heavy compression a tiny "memory" can take a few seconds to fully recover. This is the smooth, breathing-free leveling opto compressors are known for.
  • Low frequencies push the cell a bit harder than mids, so heavy bass gets leveled a little more.
  • Tone: flat in the lows with a gentle lift at the very top (about +0.25 dB at 10 kHz, +0.8 dB at 20 kHz). While compressing, the cell adds soft 2nd and 3rd harmonics around −55 dB, and the tube stage adds more when you push Gain.

Mouse & menus

  • Drag up/down on a knob or screw to turn it; the mouse wheel works too.
  • Double-click a knob to return it to its default.
  • Click the switch to flip Limit/Compress, and the lamp for Power.
  • Right-click the panel for the menu (Open manual…).
  • Drag the bottom-right corner to resize the window; it keeps its proportions.

Technical notes

  • Formats: AU and VST3, macOS 12+, universal (Apple Silicon and Intel).
  • Stereo-linked: both channels always get the same gain reduction, so the stereo image never shifts. Mono works too.
  • Processing runs at 2× oversampling to keep the tube saturation clean. The small latency is reported to the host, which compensates automatically.
  • All settings are saved with your project.
